claims.statement: From 18 February 2027, covered LMT, EV, and industrial batteries over 2 kWh require an electronic passport, so approving a supplier or model without a usable evidence pack creates a time-bounded risk of rework and delayed market placement.

The economic operator placing the finished battery on the market is responsible for creating and maintaining the passport, identifying the likely buyer for a pre-approval evidence check but not proving willingness to buy it.

A concrete but unproven control path is a 12-month nonexclusive workflow-integration agreement that places a portable evidence acceptance check before the operator approves a supplier or battery model; no customer authorization or agreement is secured.

EU rules prohibit an authorized service operator from selling, reusing, or processing passport data beyond the necessary service, so the redesign keeps outputs customer-controlled and does not depend on a cross-customer data resale moat.

A publicly funded test environment identifies data-management and infrastructure adaptation as a particular SME challenge, while its free scenarios and templates also reduce defensibility from basic completeness checking.

Siemens and Minespider already cover passport creation, validation, evidence storage, audit, and integration, so the redesign narrows the offer to a pre-procurement, platform-neutral evidence acceptance deliverable rather than another hosted passport system.

commercial_mechanics.budget_owner: Compliance, quality, procurement, product, operations, or the managing director at the responsible economic operator
commercial_mechanics.bundling_resistance: A bounded procurement-stage acceptance event, customer-hosted workspace, and platform-neutral export reduce switching friction, but incumbents and public tools can reproduce the workflow and no durable resistance is yet evidenced
commercial_mechanics.customer_relationship_owner: The economic operator owns the supplier and market relationships; the venture would own only the delivery relationship granted by a signed engagement, and none is currently secured
commercial_mechanics.distribution_origin: Proposed nonexclusive referrals or co-delivery from independent testing laboratories and import advisers, with targeted technical account outreach as the unproven fallback

fully_loaded_economics.acquisition_cost: Targeted account research, a technical readiness workshop, and any laboratory or adviser referral share; acceptance, conversion, cycle length, and total CAC remain unknown
fully_loaded_economics.cash_conversion: Proposed 50% deposit at scope lock and 50% on delivery of the evidence acceptance pack; optional annual support prepaid, with no per-unit receivable or lifetime hosting reserve
fully_loaded_economics.contribution_margin: Potentially more predictable than managed hosting because each engagement is bounded, but supplier exception cycles and analyst hours remain unmeasured and can erase margin
fully_loaded_economics.delivery_and_support_costs: Applicability mapping, document extraction, supplier evidence review, exception triage, customer calls, final portable export, and limited post-delivery corrections
fully_loaded_economics.overhead_and_compliance: Security, privacy, legal updates, professional liability, and workflow QA remain; continuous registry operation, signing, backup, migration, and durable-hosting obligations are excluded
fully_loaded_economics.revenue_basis: Unvalidated hypothesis of 12,000-25,000 PLN per supplier/model evidence acceptance sprint plus 24,000-60,000 PLN per year for the optional deployed workflow and support
fully_loaded_economics.variable_costs: Document processing, secure temporary workspace, validation labor, supplier exception handling, partner share, and bounded support; no per-unit hosting cost

commercial_mechanics.likely_incumbent_response: DPP platforms, ERP vendors, and certifier-platform alliances can add a supplier acceptance module or bundle the check into broader implementation work
commercial_mechanics.paid_event_or_measurable_loss: The paid event is delivery of a signed, portable supplier/model evidence acceptance pack and quantified gap report before supplier or model approval; measurable loss is a blocked or reworked launch after incomplete evidence is accepted
commercial_mechanics.payer: The economic operator responsible for placing the finished covered battery on the EU market
commercial_mechanics.purchase_trigger: A new supplier, component configuration, or covered battery model reaches procurement approval while required passport evidence is incomplete or unverified
commercial_mechanics.renewal_event: A new supplier or model, a material supplier or field change, or an optional annual renewal of the embedded validation workflow; automatic annual retention is not assumed

contrary_evidence: No smaller target operator is evidenced as having paid or budgeted for this exact procurement-stage evidence acceptance offer.
The operator retains statutory responsibility, passport control, and supplier relationships; the venture has no current contract, data right, or approval authority.
Supplier duties do not establish that every required field will be authentic, complete, timely, or directly accessible to this service.
Public guidance and validation scenarios reduce the scarcity of basic schema and completeness work.
Siemens, Minespider, and certifier-platform alliances can bundle or copy upstream evidence validation.
Referral conversion, delivery hours, contribution margin, repeat frequency, and the founder wealth path remain unknown.

critical_control_point.acquisition_instrument: Proposed 12-month nonexclusive workflow-integration agreement authorizing validation within a customer-controlled workspace, specifying a supplier/model evidence acceptance checklist, and requiring portable exports; no agreement is secured
critical_control_point.counterparty_refusal_fallback: Deliver a one-off offline evidence-gap audit from an operator-supplied export; if a supplier refuses data, issue a field-level missing-evidence and escalation report and do not represent the pack as complete
critical_control_point.current_owner: The responsible economic operator owns the procurement approval decision, supplier relationship, underlying information, and legal duty
critical_control_point.customer_relationship_owner: The economic operator owns the supplier and market relationships; the venture would own only the delivery relationship granted by a signed engagement, and none is currently secured
critical_control_point.duration: Proposed fixed 12-month term, renewable annually; no term is currently secured
critical_control_point.founder_access_description: Public regulation, Commission guidance, and public validation resources support an initial checklist; customer and supplier information would be used only under an operator-authorized engagement, none of which is currently held
critical_control_point.launch_controller: The responsible economic operator's procurement, quality, or compliance owner who can insert the acceptance check before supplier or model approval
critical_control_point.renewal: Optional annual workflow-support renewal plus separately scoped supplier/model acceptance sprints
critical_control_point.subject: The procurement-stage acceptance decision for a supplier or battery-model evidence pack

economics.acquisition_route: Targeted outreach to smaller covered economic operators plus proposed nonexclusive referrals from independent battery testing laboratories and import advisers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Conditional multi-year path: 100 founder-owned customer accounts at 60,000 PLN blended annual sprint and support revenue would produce 6 million PLN annual revenue; at an unproven 30% operating margin and three-times operating-profit value, the business could be worth about 5.4 million PLN before personal cash. Reach, price, margin, retention, and valuation are all unproven.
economics.founder_time: One tightly scoped pilot at a time can be attempted within 3-5 hours daily; repeat delivery requires templates and an analyst before concurrent supplier exception work exceeds that limit
economics.gross_margin_basis: Fixed sprint and optional support revenue less validation labor, exception cycles, secure workspace, legal updates, insurance, partner share, and bounded post-delivery support; continuous hosting and migration reserves are excluded
economics.payback: Customer payback is avoiding approval of a supplier or model whose missing evidence later causes launch delay or rework; no quantified loss or payback benchmark is evidenced
economics.pricing: Unvalidated hypothesis: 12,000-25,000 PLN per supplier/model acceptance sprint, with optional 24,000-60,000 PLN annual workflow support and no per-unit hosting fee
economics.retention_or_repeat: Repeat comes from new suppliers, new battery models, material data changes, and optional annual workflow support; update frequency and renewal are unknown

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Customer-specific applicability mappings, supplier exception playbooks, and review history inside each customer's controlled workspace can shorten later acceptance cycles without cross-customer passport-data reuse
fingerprint.customer: Smaller EU economic operators that are about to approve a supplier or covered e-bike, e-scooter, home-storage, EV, or industrial battery model
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Nonexclusive laboratory or import-adviser referrals plus targeted technical outreach, with no exclusive channel assumed
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A fixed-fee, customer-hosted supplier/model evidence acceptance sprint that produces a signed portable pack and gap report, plus optional annual validation-workflow support without passport hosting
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The responsible economic operator pays when a supplier/model evidence pack is accepted or rejected before procurement approval, not per unit-year of passport hosting
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A supplier, component configuration, or covered battery model is approaching procurement approval, but the operator cannot yet show that every applicable passport field has authentic, usable evidence

founder_fit: Applicability mapping, data lineage, anomaly detection, and evidence validation match the founder's data-science background
The battery and industrial context aligns with renewable-energy interests and can use Polish and EU market familiarity
A deposit-funded, fixed-scope sprint can be tested one customer at a time within the founder's five-hour daily ceiling
Technical account outreach and partner referrals avoid dependence on an on-camera personal brand
Customer-hosted delivery lowers the capital and continuous operational burden relative to running a regulated long-lived passport platform

redesign.economic_effect: Replaces per-unit passport hosting and its long-lived infrastructure, support, and liability reserve with deposit-funded fixed-price supplier/model acceptance sprints and optional annual workflow support. This lowers initial capital and open-ended cost exposure but sacrifices assumed recurring unit revenue; acquisition cost, delivery hours, margin, and renewal remain unproven.

risks: No operator may pay for a separate pre-procurement evidence gate when public tools or an incumbent platform are available
A supplier can still withhold or provide unreliable information, leaving the operator unable to approve a complete pack
Incumbents and certifier-platform alliances can bundle the same workflow and capture the referral channel
Supplier exception labor can exceed fixed-fee scope and make contribution margin negative
A customer may treat the output as compliance assurance despite explicit scope limits, creating professional-liability exposure
The founder may exceed the five-hour daily ceiling before templates and delegated delivery are proven

structural_signature.commercial_model_descriptor: fixed fee per supplier or model evidence acceptance sprint plus optional annual workflow support
structural_signature.control_point_descriptor: pre procurement evidence acceptance gate before the operator approves a supplier or covered battery model
structural_signature.critical_dependency_descriptor: the operator must enforce the evidence schedule and suppliers must deliver authentic complete updateable inputs

structure.commercial_archetype: Productized evidence-readiness and acceptance service priced per supplier or battery-model sprint
structure.control_point: A customer-authorized evidence acceptance gate embedded before supplier or model approval, with portable customer-owned output
structure.critical_dependency: The economic operator must enforce the acceptance gate and upstream suppliers must deliver authentic, complete, timely evidence

thesis: Sell smaller EU battery importers, assemblers, and product operators a fixed-scope supplier/model evidence acceptance sprint before they approve a supplier or covered battery model. Under a proposed workflow-integration agreement, validate the applicable passport fields in a customer-controlled workspace, return a signed portable evidence pack and gap report, and stop before registry submission or long-lived hosting. The operator retains legal responsibility, data control, supplier leverage, and its choice of DPP platform; the venture is paid for preventing incomplete evidence from crossing the procurement gate.
title: Battery Supplier Evidence Acceptance Gate for Small Economic Operators
uncertainties: Whether any smaller Polish or regional responsible economic operator will pay for a separate procurement-stage evidence acceptance sprint
Whether an operator will insert the proposed gate into supplier or model approval and sign the necessary authorization
Whether suppliers can provide authentic, complete, timely, and updateable values for every applicable field
Referral willingness, lead volume, conversion, sales-cycle length, and channel share for independent laboratories and import advisers
Realized extraction hours, exception cycles, secure-workspace cost, support load, insurance cost, contribution margin, and cash conversion
Repeat frequency across suppliers and models and willingness to renew optional annual workflow support
Whether platform-neutral positioning survives bundling by DPP platforms, ERP vendors, and certifier-platform alliances
Whether the operation can remain within five founder hours daily until templates and delegated analyst delivery are proven
Whether reachable accounts and contribution economics can support the stated founder net-worth path
